title: Reading 130
paragraphs: And thus, Glaucon, the tale has been saved and has not perished, and will save us if we are obedient to the word spoken; and we shall pass safely over the river of Forgetfulness and our soul will not be defiled. Wherefore my counsel is, that we hold fast ever to the heavenly way and follow after justice and virtue always, considering that the soul is immortal and able to endure every sort of good and every sort of evil. Thus shall we live dear to one another and to the gods, both while remaining here and when, like conquerors in the games who go round to gather gifts, we receive our reward. And it shall be well with us both in this life and in the pilgrimage of a thousand years which we have been describing.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of obeying the spoken word according to the text?
options: To gain material wealth.
To pass safely over the river of Forgetfulness.
To prove that the soul is mortal.
To avoid conflict with other conquerors.
quiz.explanation: The text states that obeying the word spoken will save them and allow them to pass safely over the river of Forgetfulness.

quiz.question: What is the author's counsel regarding the path to follow?
options: To seek only earthly rewards.
To hold fast ever to the heavenly way.
To focus solely on material gifts.
To ignore the concept of justice.
quiz.explanation: The text advises that they should hold fast ever to the heavenly way and follow after justice and virtue always.

quiz.question: According to the passage, why is the soul considered immortal?
options: Because it is able to endure every sort of good and every sort of evil.
Because it is capable of gathering gifts.
Because it is a conqueror in games.
Because it is able to remain here.
quiz.explanation: The text states that the soul is immortal and able to endure every sort of good and every sort of evil.

quiz.question: How does the text suggest they should live in relation to one another and the gods?
options: By competing for gifts.
By remaining here and when.
By living dear to one another and to the gods.
By focusing only on earthly rewards.
quiz.explanation: The text promises that they shall live dear to one another and to the gods.

quiz.question: What is the ultimate reward mentioned in the passage?
options: Winning material gifts.
Remaining here and when.
Receiving their reward like conquerors.
Passing safely over the river of Forgetfulness.
quiz.explanation: The text mentions that they receive their reward when they act like conquerors in the games who go round to gather gifts.
